title: Bounded Context

validation.research: Seven authoritative references: Evans’s DDD Reference establishes model applicability and Context Map relationships; Fowler explains locally unified meanings and deliberate mappings; Microsoft distinguishes context modeling from deployment units and documents translation ownership; Salesforce supplies the retained API-federation example; Python documents frozen-field behavior. Bounded Context is distinguished from a subdomain, aggregate, department, deployment, database, security boundary, and transaction boundary. Northstar and inventory scenarios are retained original teaching examples; new Python and native SVGs are original.
validation.python_examples: All three article fences execute as billing.py, access.py, and demo.py and produce the five stated lines exactly. Checks cover published-contract-only imports, local validation, nonblank opaque IDs, strict finite payment vocabulary and Boolean enabled states, exact funding identity, mismatched and unresolved mappings, immutable snapshots, both enabled states, no hidden state across repeated assessments, and one payer funding multiple distinct workspaces. No permissions or persistence are changed.
validation.article_tests: 75 article tests pass across Bounded Context and the prior software/GoF suites. The run uses two workers, 20-second test timeout, and 60-second corpus hook timeout.

example_limits: Single-process snapshot assessment only, Python 3.10+. It does not implement invoice calculation, transport, producer authentication, freshness, revision ordering, retry handling, historical crosswalks, persistence, concurrency coordination, or permission changes. Frozen fields protect normal API assignment, not authority or all possible mutation. The current/overdue interpretation is an original local teaching policy, not a guarantee of the pattern. Production mappings and coordination need explicit ownership, contracts, effective times, and failure handling.
publication: Local implementation only. No publishing, deployment, push, or pull request.
